comments.body: Superseded. The library and build jobs now run Python 3.14 on main, and the Home Assistant integration job stays on 3.13 because that is what Home Assistant runs (installing HA on 3.14 fails, which is why this PR was red). A packageRule now stops Renovate offering that job a newer Python.

body:
Converges the release pipeline with dreame-valetudo and removes every trace of QEMU emulation.

**Architecture decides the forge, and nothing is emulated.** amd64 builds and install-tests on the
Forgejo runner; arm64 and macOS on GitHub's native runners. `build-linux-arch.sh` and
`install-matrix-arch.sh` refuse to run when the host and target architectures disagree, so an
emulated build cannot come back by accident. This retires the PyInstaller 6.22.0 pin, whose only
cause was emulation, and deletes the watch script that tracked it.

**Release-path fixes found by a cold cross-repo audit:**

- the manual prune failed *open* on a malformed `dry_run`, and ran the dispatched branch's script
- the macOS signing workflow held eight secrets job-wide and never removed the decoded key files
- the `.pkg` was built on macOS 26 with no deployment target and published untested, while the
  README claims macOS 15
- the macOS toolchain was unpinned, so one release could freeze its `.pkg` and its Linux artifacts
  with different PyInstallers
- jobs carrying `always()`/`!cancelled()` ran even when the ref guard *refused* the ref, doing
  external writes with `GITHUB_REF_NAME` set to a branch name
- the repository index was matched on version alone — and the registry is owner-scoped, so
  dreame-valetudo's package at the same version could satisfy the check
- all five compat floors were unclamped and would have drifted into second current-release tests

Checksums are now per-architecture (`SHA256SUMS-$(uname -m)`), each written by the machine that
built those bytes. Users on apt/dnf, Homebrew, PyPI or macOS are unaffected — those verify
automatically and never touch this file.

**Do not cut a release from `main` until this lands:** both forges now sign with the namespace key
`CCE50015D058E9BF`, which only this branch publishes.

title: Converge the release pipeline: native arm64, no emulation, and the audit fixes

body:
The marker filename is derived from `__version__`. These tests spelled the stable marker literally, so they passed only while the checkout carried a stable version.

Every prerelease gate stamps an rc BEFORE running the suite, so the next rc cut was guaranteed to fail on them. It did: run 5843.

The fixture pins the channel and runs each affected test on both, so the channel split is now covered rather than incidentally satisfied.

The window is now sized against how long a busy forge can defer a job, and is overridable.

body:
Two invariants, both mirrored in dreame-valetudo.

**pip needs its own Python.** A job that pip-installs into the runner image's interpreter dies on PEP 668. Nothing in a workflow says which Python a step gets, so this stays invisible until an image changes under a job that worked for months. It hit dreame's tap job mid-release, after the tag was cut.

**A compatibility floor has to stay old.** Renovate cannot tell a floor from a current-release alias; unclamped it bumps the tag and the leg becomes a second current test — green, proving nothing.
head: refs/pull/25/head
title: Guard the interpreter a pip install gets, and the compatibility floors

body:
Homebrew refuses to LOAD a formula from an untrusted third-party tap. Building the rc bottle loads the stable formula too, because the rc formula's `conflicts_with` names it.

That means this only bites once a stable formula exists in the tap. dreame-valetudo has one, so every bottle job on rc.17 and rc.18 died with `Refusing to load formula ... from untrusted tap`. whiskerless has no stable formula in the tap yet, so it was passing on an absence rather than on correctness — and would have broken the first time 0.2.0 shipped.

Guarded on the subcommand existing, not on its exit status: an older Homebrew has no `trust` and needs none, while a `trust` that exists and fails is a real problem and must stop the build.

Renovate can raise the `PROJECT_STANDARD` pin but cannot fetch the tag it then names, so every standard bump landed red on the drift check and was closed as obsolete.

A candidate died on `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: astral.sh` while fetching the uv installer. The infra-retry workflow correctly declined to rescue it — the failure was inside one of our own steps, which is exactly what that workflow refuses to launder into green. So the fix belongs on the fetch.

- every network fetch in the install path now retries
- the installer is written to a file, never piped: curl cannot rewind a pipe, so a retried partial body would reach `sh` concatenated with the first
- container fetches retry in the shell via `packaging/fetch.sh`, because `--retry` alone does not cover a name-resolution failure and Rocky 8 ships curl 7.61, which rejects `--retry-all-errors` outright

rc.43 died on `dist/whiskerless: A timestamp was expected but was not found` while signing the x86_64 pkg. arm64 signed fine on the same run, so it was a transient outage at Apple.

Every macOS release step reaches an Apple service on every invocation: `codesign` and `productsign` each request a trusted timestamp, `notarytool` uploads, and `stapler` downloads the ticket back. All four now go through `packaging/retry.sh` with a backoff that spans two and a half minutes.

Dropping the timestamp was never an option - it is what keeps the signature verifiable past the certificate expiry, and notarization refuses a build without one.

The invariant derives the covered window from the script and the workflow rather than restating it, so widening one without the other cannot pass quietly.

body:
A workflow-shape audit across all 14 shared workflows, after an earlier convergence pass checked Renovate identities, action pins and install channels but never looked at triggers or concurrency.

Three divergences, each repo missing something the other had:

- `.forgejo/ci.yml` had `workflow_dispatch` in whiskerless only. Forgejo has no rerun API, so dreame main was stranded red by a cluster-wide network outage with no way back except an unrelated commit.
- `.forgejo/ci.yml` had per-ref concurrency in whiskerless only, so dreame left superseded runs competing for runners.
- `.forgejo/publish.yml` had per-tag serialisation in dreame only, so whiskerless publishing was not deduplicated at all.

Both publish groups now key on the FULL ref: `ref_name` drops refs/heads and refs/tags alike, so a branch sharing a tag name would share its group, and publish.yml is dispatchable.

Guards mirrored into both, each mutation-verified.

Re-lands the bottle mirroring reverted earlier, with the reason it was reverted actually fixed.

Setting `HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN` makes Homebrew suppress the anonymous `Authorization: Bearer QQ==` it would otherwise send to ghcr.io, so any bottle the mirror could not serve fell back bare and got a 401. `HOMEBREW_DOCKER_REGISTRY_TOKEN=QQ==` restores exactly that anonymous credential: ghcr.io answers 200 for it (verified directly) and the mirror ignores it, so a mirror miss downloads the bottle instead of failing the job.

Measured from a runner rather than a workstation: a cold entry syncs in about 21s against the roughly 7s Homebrew's default three retries allow, which is what the raised retry budget is for; a 170MB bottle already synced serves in about 2s. The repo invariant now fails if either the credential or the retry budget is dropped while a mirror is set.

body:
The mirror syncs **on demand**, so the first request for a bottle it has never seen blocks while it pulls from ghcr.io — measured at about 21s per entry from a runner, against the roughly 7s Homebrew's default three retries allow. The smoke jobs raise that budget so a cold entry survives, but it is paid again on every dependency whenever upstream rebuilds its bottles.

This walks the formula's own dependency closure with `brew deps` and fetches each bottle with `brew fetch`, which is what populates the mirror. Nothing hardcodes a formula list that could drift from what the smoke installs.

**Verified on a real runner, not asserted:** whiskerless warms 62/62 of its closure and dreame 85/85, both with zero misses.

Three things a cold review caught, each fixed and then re-tested:

- `HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN_NO_FALLBACK` is set **here only**. Without it every fetch could succeed from ghcr.io and report a warm mirror that received nothing. The smoke jobs deliberately keep the fallback, where a miss should cost latency rather than a red build.
- The **rc** formula is warmed first, and chosen by which file exists rather than by an exit code. `update-tap.sh` advances only the rc on a prerelease, so the stable formula lags — measured three dependencies short of its own rc in dreame.
- `brew trust` is applied as the install smoke does; without it, reading a third-party formula exits non-zero even when it printed the formula correctly, which silently selected the stale closure.

**Known limit, stated in the workflow:** the closure comes from the published tap, so a dependency newly added to the local formula template is not warm until a release publishes it. The first job to want it pays one cold sync, which the raised retry budget already absorbs.
head: refs/pull/39/head
title: Warm the bottle mirror daily

body:
The formula job proved current arm64 and nothing else, while `ci-macos.yml` holds the library to four lanes. Both formulae compile native code on the installing machine — a Rust extension in whiskerless, `sunxi-tools` built with `make sunxi-fel` here — so a break can be specific to Intel or to the macOS floor. The bottle build does cover those lanes, but only at tag time, and a tag is immutable by the time it reports.

Four lanes of a job that compiles is not cheap. Killing this workflow's duplicate `pull_request` run earlier paid for half of it; the rest buys the only coverage that was missing.

A new invariant fails if the two lane sets ever diverge again, in either direction.
head: refs/pull/40/head
title: Build the formula on every macOS lane the library is tested on

body:
The Linux suites were the whole CI verdict; macOS ran only on the mirror. A pull request could therefore read green with its macOS matrix red, and nothing noticed until the release gate refused to tag — by which point the commit was already on main. dreame-valetudo has held this gate for a while; this ports it.

Three things the review caught, each fixed and then mutation-tested:

- **It must not run for a tag.** A prerelease stamps a commit pushed only as a tag, and `ci-macos.yml` runs on branch pushes — so no run could ever exist for that sha and the gate would poll to timeout and fail *every prerelease*. dreame escapes this only because its `ci.yml` has no tag trigger; whiskerless's does.
- **No write credential.** The checkout persisted the repository token where a script from a PR-controlled ref runs beside it. Now `persist-credentials: false`, matching the release mirror gate.
- **The guard was inert.** An over-escaped pattern matched a literal backslash and never fired. It now catches write-capable secrets in upper *and* lower case.

Second commit is unrelated bookkeeping: the backlog index still advertised #85/#86 as open work while their own sections record them closed on 2026-08-20.

5d07h from Loki (08-19 21:11Z → 08-25 04:52Z): 1,065,899 lines → 47,655 records, 0 malformed → 17,359 readings over 7,322 payload seconds.

**`0x6D` emits from inside the sweep's only silent gap.** `registers.md` records that a paced sweep answered 123 of 128 addresses and that the sole gap is `0x6A`–`0x6E`. `0x6D` is in it — it answered no read, yet pushed six readings in nine minutes. The file already warns that a silent register proves nothing on its own; this is the direct evidence for that warning.

**The unlisted registers split by MAIN-BOARD firmware on identical hardware.** Same `espFirmware=1.1.75`, same `mbHardware`/`mbBom`/`mbSuite`, but `mbRevision` 89/build 1 emits `0x6D`+`0x71` while 93/build 2 emits `0x67`. A clean correlation on n=2, and cheap to test: when a board updates, its registers should switch sets. This corrects #19's open question rather than contradicting it.

**The lead did not advance.** No `0x5F`–`0x63` and no `0x35` in 5d07h, so ~9d05h clean. Consistent with the fault-coupled reading, not support for it — a `0x35` fault *without* the five is what would refute it.

**Three method corrections**, each caught in review after I got it wrong first:
- `kubectl logs --since-time` returned five MINUTES against a 5d23h pod: the container log had rotated. The standing rule needed a third condition.
- Three claims of undocumented registers were wrong because `registers.md` uses RANGES that a literal search for `0x3E` does not match. Only `0x0C` is genuinely missing.
- The canonical METHOD RULE omitted the serial from the dedupe key. For a pass spanning both robots that can collapse two devices into one reading and manufacture the exclusivity this correlation rests on. The analysis did include it; the rule now says so.

body:
`v0.3.0-rc.27` lost its bottles, and the install matrix that waits on them, to a **sixty-second** miss.

`build-bottles.sh` waits for publish.yml's first tap pass; publish.yml's second pass then waits for the bottles built here. That handshake is correct and unchanged. What failed was the budget: `90 x 20s` = **30 minutes**, against a publish that took **37m18s** to write the formula (started 16:45:56Z, tap pass landed 17:23:12Z). The loop gave up at 17:22:12Z. The formula appeared one minute later.

The same publish has reached the tap inside 17 minutes on other runs, so the spread is wide and 30 minutes sat inside it. Now `270 x 20s` = 90 minutes.

**Widening is close to free.** The loop breaks the moment the formula appears, so the budget is a FAILURE bound rather than a delay: it costs nothing on a healthy release and a longer red run when publishing is genuinely broken.

**This applies to stable too.** `bottles.yml` triggers on `v*.*.*`, so `v0.3.0` races exactly as the rc did — and stable's publish does more before the tap pass, while a stable tag is permanent. `retry-infra-failures` would not have saved it either: it re-runs *infrastructure* failures, and `::error::the tap never published…` is an application-level failure it correctly declines.

A new invariant fails if the budget drops under 60 minutes, mutation-tested against both factors — fewer iterations and a shorter sleep. The failure message now names the recovery dispatch.

body:
A dropped connection to one forge failed a whole release leg. Three things turned that transient into a terminal error:

- `rel_asset_state` returned `1` both for "the request failed" and for "the metadata is unreadable", so a reset was indistinguishable from a real byte conflict. It now returns `12` for a failed request.
- `rel_verify_uploaded_asset` retried `10` (not visible yet) but returned immediately on `1`. That is what actually failed the last bottle publish: the upload succeeded, the *verify read* was reset, and a failed lookup was treated as a verdict. It now keeps looking on `12`.
- Uploads had no retry at all. `rel_upload_verified` now retries, and re-checks forge state before every attempt, so a write that landed before the connection broke is recognised rather than repeated. No upload is issued without a definite ABSENT verdict.

Retried reads are also written to a file curl can truncate rather than a stdout it cannot rewind, so a body reset mid-response cannot be concatenated with its replacement and parsed as malformed JSON.

`REL_MUTATE` still carries no curl-level retry, which stays correct: curl cannot tell a write that never landed from one that landed and lost its reply. The retry belongs one level up, where it can look first.

Vendored from project-standard v0.1.17. Covered by six new unit tests (each mutation-tested) and the existing release integration suite on both forges.

body:
A mirror that drops a connection mid-fetch is not this project failing, but apt treats it as fatal and the whole install leg goes red for it — observed on `ports.ubuntu.com` during the rc.48 arm64 matrix, where `deb-file-ubuntu` and `deb-file-ubuntu-floor` both died on `Failed to fetch`.

Retries are set as apt POLICY (`Acquire::Retries "3"` in `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/`) in every stage that runs `apt-get update`, so all derived stages inherit it and a new leg cannot forget.

Deliberately NOT done by widening `triage-infra-failure.py`: that script only treats runner-phase failures as infrastructure, and its own reasoning is that broadening it would become a way to launder flaky tests into green builds. Making the fetch survive the network is a different thing from excusing a failure — a package that genuinely does not install still fails.

Verified in a real ubuntu:22.04 arm64 container (`apt-config dump` shows the policy active, install succeeds). The new invariant asserts no `apt-get update` exists without the policy, and refuses to pass if its own scan finds nothing.
head: refs/pull/50/head
title: Let apt retry a dropped mirror fetch

body:
The Linux install matrix triggered on the tag push — the same instant `publish.yml` starts — so its wait job held one of the runner's few slots for its entire budget, polling for artifacts the publish it was starving had not built yet. Measured on rc.48: the publish pipeline did ~14 minutes of real work but took 50, with 15- and 21-minute gaps where no publish job was running at all.

Forgejo has no `workflow_run`, so the finished publish now says so explicitly: `install-matrix.yml` is dispatch-only, and `publish.yml` hands it the tag after every producer plus `reconcile` settles.

It runs even when a producer reported failure, deliberately: a destination can fail its upload and `reconcile` can then heal the release across registries, leaving a COMPLETE release whose handoff had been skipped — a release with no install matrix at all. `wait-for-release.sh` remains the authority on whether the release is genuinely installable.

Also pins a gap neither project had covered: nothing asserted that `build-linux-arch.sh` smokes BOTH package formats before publish, so the `.rpm` gate could have been dropped without anything noticing.

The GitHub half deliberately stays on tag push — it runs on GitHub-hosted runners, so its waiting does not starve this runner, and a trigger that cannot silently fail is worth more there.
head: refs/pull/51/head
title: Start the install matrix when the release is ready

body:
The README is a promise — "tested on every minimum version below" — and nothing checked it. Seven claims had drifted from what any lane actually runs:

- The `.rpm` was never installed on the oldest maintained Fedora, only upgrade-tested from source in the pre-merge ladder. Now a real install lane.
- openSUSE Leap 15.6 was already install-tested while the table named 16.0 as the minimum, understating real coverage.
- Windows is claimed to work; nothing tests it. Now stated plainly rather than implied.
- RHEL and Raspberry Pi OS are named but have no lane — RHEL has no public image to install into, Raspberry Pi OS is Debian 12 underneath. Both are covered by inheritance, and now the README says so.

The invariant that replaces the guesswork parses the support table, resolves the Dockerfile stage graph down from the channel list, and asserts every promised version has a channel that really installs the shipped package on it. Text-searching the Dockerfile was not enough: a pinned-but-unused base looks identical to a tested one, which is exactly the Fedora gap.

Two systems carry no version number, so the parse structurally cannot see them — their disclaimers are pinned separately.

Also fixes a lane that reported success while testing very little: the new Fedora base installed only curl, so `installed-smoke.sh` took its no-openssl branch and skipped every certificate, backup and restore check while still printing PASS.
head: refs/pull/52/head
title: Make the README promises match what is actually tested

body:
The install matrix was the tail of every release. Two changes, measured rather than guessed.

**Both halves now start the same way.** The GitHub matrix triggered on the tag push — the same instant publish starts — and spent ~22 minutes waiting for artifacts that did not exist yet. Unlike the Forgejo case this starved nothing (its runners were free, and every leg started within seconds of the artifacts landing), so it buys no wall clock. It is for consistency: one mechanism starts both halves, and a mechanism that differs per forge is how the two drift apart. `publish.yml` now dispatches both.

**Both Linux legs are sharded.** The channels are independent and were only sequential by default. Measured on a real dispatch against v0.2.0-rc.51: the arm64 leg went from **33 minutes to 7m24s**, four shards balanced at 4m54s / 5m40s / 5m00s / 7m24s. The whole GitHub matrix dropped from 33 to 20 minutes; what remains is macOS **Intel** runners queueing ~15 minutes for capacity, which no workflow change reaches.

Shard counts differ per forge on purpose, the same way `CACHE_CEILING_GB` already does: GitHub gets four, Forgejo gets **two**, because that pool is exactly four self-hosted runners. Four shards there would take all of them — blocking the sibling project’s publish and every PR check — to speed up a leg measured at 8–14 minutes against GitHub’s 20+, which is not the critical path and so would not move the release at all.

An invariant pins the declared shard list against the count handed to the script. Passing four while declaring two would leave half the channels unselected, the shards that ran passing, and the architecture reported green having installed half of what it publishes.

**Note for whoever merges:** the GitHub dispatch needs `Actions: read & write` on `GH_REPO_WRITE_PAT`, which previously held Contents only. The requirement is now documented in `packaging/README.md`. If it is missing the handoff fails loudly within a second rather than silently skipping, and the matrix stays dispatchable by hand with a tag input.

title: Start both install matrices from one handoff, and shard them

body:
The earlier answer to #21 blamed a marginal WiFi link. That was wrong, and a confident wrong answer in the permanent record is worse than the blocked state it replaced.

The broker log shows the robot dropped on keepalive timeout, retried twice, aborted both retries mid-TLS-handshake, then stopped trying for ten hours — while answering ICMP with 0% loss. Robot-side, not broker-side: the sibling robot handshook against the same broker three hours later, and the cert is valid into 2036.

wifiRssi is bimodal on both robots and resamples per MQTT session, but inter-message cadence is identical in both clusters, so it did not explain this incident. The text is careful not to overcorrect into claiming the field is meaningless — it is a real measurement that is not a diagnosis on its own.

Also adds #90: telling a robot that has left the broker apart from one merely not answering, with the inference direction hedged (silence alone cannot prove it).

body:
Follow-ups to the guard added with the audit fixes, all found by review:

- hyphen and Cisco-dotted spellings were not matched at all
- a fixed six-group pattern read the tail of an IPv6 address written with variable-width hextets as an address, and the head of a longer byte run such as 01-02-...-08
- a short hex-looking label glued to the front (id:, or the trailing letters of mac:) made the whole token fail the two-digit test and vanish

Now: maximal run per separator, judged by shape. Six two-digit groups is an address; seven is a label glued to one and is ambiguous about which end, so both readings are offered and the allowlist decides; eight or more is a byte sequence or IPv6. Bare packed hex is deliberately NOT matched — the sibling tree carries 156 distinct twelve-hex tokens, so that rule would fail every run and the guard would be deleted.

body:
Two gaps behind the same symptom that failed rc.41.

`prerelease.yml` deliberately does NOT call `packaging/push-tag.sh` - it inlines the tag push because that step is where the repo-write PAT reaches shell and the workflow is dispatchable from any branch, so it must not execute a script read back off the checkout. The consequence was that v0.1.22's mirror confirmation never reached the path that actually cuts rcs. The verification half needs no credential, so it goes inline as workflow-defined text: an unauthenticated GET against a slug the runner supplies.

And confirming by HTTP status alone was not enough. An rc number is derived from the source tags, so a name is reusable, and a ref left behind by a partial prune answers 200 while still pointing at the previous release. Both the inline copy and the shared helper now compare the object the mirror serves with the one just pushed (project-standard v0.1.23, vendored here).

The POST is bounded too - unbounded, a stalled sync would have prevented the readback from ever running.

body:
Reproduced on v0.3.0-rc.44: its tap job failed `! [rejected] main -> main (fetch first)` because whiskerless rc.65 wrote the shared tap first.

The hazard was already documented at the job - "three jobs write this one repository, and two of them cloning the same tip means the loser pushes a non-fast-forward" - and the mitigation was `concurrency: group: tap-write`. But a concurrency group is scoped to one repository, so it cannot serialise the SIBLING, and both projects publish into `SisyphusMD/homebrew-tap`.

All six writer sites across the two repos (publish.yml pass 1 and pass 2, tap-bottles.yml, in each) now fetch, rebase onto the new tip and retry. Each project renders only its own formula file, so replaying is the correct resolution; a conflict means a genuine collision and still fails loudly.

body:
Rewriting history moves every tag at once, and publish.yml fires on tag pushes, so one rewrite queues one publish run per tag. That happened here today: 35 runs, each rebuilding an already-shipped rc for roughly twenty minutes before the immutable-asset policy refused it on all three hosts.

Nothing was overwritten - that guard did its job - but the refusal is knowable in seconds. This checks whether the tag already has a release before any build starts.

Scoped to `push`, because a dispatch is the documented way to FINISH a partial publish and every helper it runs is idempotent. Read unauthenticated from the mirror, so it needs no secret in a job that deliberately checks out without credentials. Inconclusive answers do not block: a rate-limited probe refusing a legitimate release would be worse than a wasted build, and the immutable-asset refusal is still the backstop.

Exercised against the live API on all four branches - an existing release refuses, an unknown tag proceeds, a stubbed 5xx warns and continues.

body:
Vendors project-standard v0.1.24 and lands the workflow half.

**No unauthenticated GitHub calls.** Unauthenticated github.com allows 60 requests an hour per IP and every runner, mirror probe and CI poller shares one. Several helpers treated their token as optional, so once that budget was gone they did not fail - they answered 403, and the checks built on them stopped deciding anything while still reporting success. push-tag.sh, check-mirror-ci.sh, check-rc-install-matrix.sh, reconcile-releases.sh, github-release.sh and wait-for-release.sh now all make the token mandatory; reconcile also authenticates the asset download, which was going out bare.

push-tag.sh asserts before `git push --atomic`, and prerelease.yml asserts in the push step rather than the mirror step two steps later, because discovering it afterwards leaves the tag published and the run failed.

**The republish guard.** A history rewrite moves every tag at once and publish.yml fires on tag pushes, so one rewrite queues one publish run per tag - 35 of them here, each rebuilding a shipped rc for ~20 minutes before the immutable-asset policy refused it. The guard now checks BOTH publication targets before any build: checking only the source of truth would answer 404 for a partial publish that reached GitHub alone, and let a rewritten tag write new bytes to Forgejo and the NAS before GitHub refused them. It retries a non-definitive answer and then fails closed, since that is precisely when the inconsistency happens; a dispatch with the tag as the ref remains the escape, and is still the way to finish a partial publish.

Exercised against the live forge and mirror: a published tag refuses, an unknown tag proceeds, an unreachable forge and a bad credential both refuse.

body:
GitHub run 35055059591 stayed red: `brew test` bootstrapped Homebrew's Ruby harness and the x86_64 macOS runner could not resolve rubygems.org. The failure landed in our named step, so the step-name rule refused the retry.

Vendors project-standard v0.1.25, whose discriminator now reads each failed job's log and retries only when the failed step's own closing lines carry an exact resolver-failure spelling and name a host CI is known to reach. The workflow downloads one log per failed job (`gh api --allow-escape-sequences`, without which `gh` refuses ANSI-coloured bodies) and passes the directory through. The invariant test pins the fetch and the flag, and the sibling's `the triage is the shared one` test is mirrored here, which whiskerless had been missing.

Same change lands in dreame-valetudo.

| [ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff) ([source](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff), [changelog](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)) | `==0.16.10` → `==0.17.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/ruff/0.17.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/ruff/0.16.10/0.17.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/ruff (ruff)</summary>

### [`v0.17.0`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0170)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/compare/0.16.10...0.17.0)

Released on 2026-10-09.

The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and `ruff` wheels are now code-signed.
macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows
executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables
verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting,
and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.

##### Breaking changes

- Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 ([#​28792](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28792))

  Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through
  [`target-version`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#target-version) or
  [`requires-python`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/#inferring-the-python-version). When
  checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15
  instead of 3.14.

- Update the default rule set ([#​28786](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28786))

  Several of the `flake8-datetimez` rules
  ([`DTZ001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-without-tzinfo/),
  [`DTZ005`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-now-without-tzinfo/),
  [`DTZ006`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-fromtimestamp/),
  [`DTZ007`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-strptime-without-zone/),
  [`DTZ011`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-date-today/),
  [`DTZ012`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-date-fromtimestamp/), and
  [`DTZ901`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/datetime-min-max/)) are no longer enabled by default,
  while [`undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage/)
  (`F406`), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.

- Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 ([#​27295](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27295))

  JUnit output now uses a `skipped` attribute instead of `disabled` on `<testsuite>` elements and
  includes a `skipped` attribute on the root `<testsuites>` element.

- \[`flake8-import-conventions`] Add `datetime as dt` as a conventional alias (`ICN001`) ([#​28790](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28790))

- Support Unicode dummy variable names ([#​28722](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28722))

  The default [`lint.dummy-variable-rgx`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_dummy-variable-rgx)
  now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as `_次`, as dummy variables.

- Update to Unicode 17 ([#​21229](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21229), [#​28784](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28784))

  Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes (`"\N{...}"`).

- Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI ([#​27810](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27810))

  The default `full` output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review,
  regardless of the [`unsafe-fixes`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#unsafe-fixes) setting.
  Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.

- Remove the Python dependency from conda-forge builds ([conda-forge/ruff-feedstock#361](https://github.com/conda-forge/ruff-feedstock/pull/361))

  The conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, now supports linux-riscv64, win-arm64, and
  linux-ppc64le platforms, and now includes shell completions. However, no longer depending on
  Python means that `python -m ruff` and `import ruff` will no longer work. Use `ruff` directly from
  `PATH` instead. PyPI installations and those from the standalone installer are unaffected.

- Remove support for ruff-lsp ([#​28750](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28750))

  Support for `ruff-lsp`, the legacy Python language server [deprecated in Ruff
  v0.9.5](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/releases/tag/0.9.5), has been removed. The Ruff VS Code
  extension now always uses the native language server; `ruff.nativeServer` is deprecated and
  ignored. See the [migration guide](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/editors/migration/).

##### Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

- [`lazy-import-mismatch`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/lazy-import-mismatch) (`TID254`)
- [`lazy-import-immediately-resolved`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/lazy-import-immediately-resolved)
  (`TID255`)
- [`os-path-commonprefix`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/os-path-commonprefix) (`RUF071`)

The following behaviors have been stabilized:

- The formatter, [`unsorted-imports`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unsorted-imports/) (`I001`),
  [`line-too-long`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/line-too-long/) (`E501`), and
  [`doc-line-too-long`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/doc-line-too-long/) (`W505`) now
  consistently ignore trailing pragma comments when computing line length. This resolved several
  bugs involving interactions between these rules
  ([#​27313](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27313)) but may also cause existing imports to be
  reformatted and was thus classified as a breaking change.

##### Preview features

- \[`flake8-bugbear`] Report the method name and a more precise range (`B005`) ([#​27050](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27050))
- \[`refurb`] Mark fix unsafe and move to `suspicious` (`FURB152`) ([#​28405](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28405))
- \[`ruff`] Allow docstrings in strict mode (`RUF067`) ([#​28679](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28679))

##### Bug fixes

- \[`flake8-builtins`] Expand checks in class scopes (`A001`) ([#​29076](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29076))
- \[`flake8-self`] Allow private access on `object.__new__(cls)` instances (`SLF001`) ([#​29001](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29001))
- \[`flake8-tidy-imports`] Skip `lazy-import-mismatch` in stubs (`TID254`) ([#​29095](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29095))
- \[`flake8-type-checking`] Add the notion of runtime-ambiguous references ([#​26508](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/26508))
- \[`flake8-type-checking`] Never flag annotations in function scopes ([#​29183](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29183))
- \[`pyflakes`] Mark the fix as unsafe when it creates a docstring (`F541`) ([#​28258](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28258))
- \[`pylint`] Preserve trailing comments in `useless-return` fix (`PLR1711`) ([#​29180](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29180))
- \[`ruff`] Avoid false positive when `pytest.raises` is used in a `with` statement (`RUF061`) ([#​28186](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28186))

- \[`pyupgrade`] Suggest `typing.TypeForm` on Python 3.15 (`UP035`) ([#​29084](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29084))

body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---| | [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) ([changelog](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/changelog.html)) | `==9.1.1` → `==9.2.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/pytest/9.2.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/pytest/9.1.1/9.2.0?slim=true) | --- ### Release Notes
pytest-dev/pytest (pytest) ### [`v9.2.0`](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/releases/tag/9.2.0) [Compare Source](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/9.1.1...9.2.0) ### pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27) #### Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes - [#​14716](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14716): `-c` now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled `FileNotFoundError`. - [#​8593](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8593): The `indirect`, `ids` and `scope` arguments of `Metafunc.parametrize() ` -- and therefore of `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` -- are now keyword-only. Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. `parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)])` made the argvalues land in `indirect` and failed with `indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist`; such mistakes now fail with an understandable `TypeError`. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only. - [#​993](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/993): Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code `1`: - a plugin that cannot be found -- via `-p`, `pytest_plugins` or `PYTEST_PLUGINS` -- exits with `pytest.ExitCode` `USAGE_ERROR` (`4`), like a `conftest.py` that fails to import; - a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken `pytest11` entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with `pytest.ExitCode` `INTERNAL_ERROR` (`3`), with the traceback preserved. `pytest.main` now returns these codes instead of raising `ImportError`. Also fixed an `IndexError` from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments. #### Deprecations (removal in next major release) - [#​14742](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14742): The private `_pytest.python.CallSpec2` name has been renamed to `CallSpec`. The old `CallSpec2` alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11. - [#​14755](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14755): Schedule *yield_fixture* decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11. - [#​14774](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14774): Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, *all* higher-scoped fixtures (`module`, `package`, and `session`) defined as instance methods are now deprecated. They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see `10819` and `14011`. - [#​14808](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14808): Passing a non-string value to a `string`-typed ini option now emits a `pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning`. This affects `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml`. In pytest 10 this will raise a `TypeError`, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path. - [#​7323](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7323): Passing `bytes` to `TerminalReporter.write_line()` is now deprecated, pass a `str` instead. #### New features - [#​14743](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14743): Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output. - [#​2781](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2781): When `strict_markers` is enabled, marker names used in `-m` expressions are now validated against registered markers. - [#​6881](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6881): Added the `parametrize_long_str_id_strategy` configuration option to control how long `str`/`bytes` parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via `ids=[...]` or `pytest.param(..., id=...)` are not affected. Available strategies: `short` (default, values over 100 chars fall back to `argname+index`), `sha256` (SHA-256 hex digest), `legacy` (keep full value), and `disallow` (error requesting explicit IDs). #### Improvements in existing functionality - [#​10745](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745): A `RecursionError` whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass `--full-trace` to see every frame. - [#​10745](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745): The line numbers of a module's statements are now computed once per traceback instead of once per traceback entry, which noticeably speeds up rendering failures raised from large test modules. - [#​11418](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11418): The cached rewritten modules in `__pycache__` are now invalidated by a hash of the source instead of its modification time, using the checked-hash pyc format from `552`. Timestamps make the cache useless wherever source files get fresh modification times, most notably in CI: a checkout gives every file a new mtime, so a restored cache is discarded in full and every test module is rewritten again. Hashing the source costs roughly 15 microseconds per file and makes the cache survive that. Existing timestamp based caches are ignored and rewritten once. - [#​12624](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12624): The `pytest_plugins` variable and the `PYTEST_PLUGINS` environment variable now also accept entry point names of installed plugins (e.g. `xdist`), in addition to importable module names, matching the behavior of the `-p` command-line option. As part of this change, plugins specified by entry point name through these mechanisms are now also listed in the `plugins:` line of the terminal header (`12615`). Based on the original implementation by Marcel Telka in `12616`. - [#​12697](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12697): Warnings emitted while importing plugins through `-p`, `PYTEST_PLUGINS`, or entry point autoloading are now captured, filtered, and reported like other warnings. - [#​12860](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12860): Assertion diffs for `dict.items()` and `dict.keys()` comparisons (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `==`) now show which items are missing, the same way set comparisons do. - [#​13354](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13354): `Node.get_closest_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.get_closest_marker>` now also accepts a `~pytest.MarkDecorator` as its `default`, for example `item.get_closest_marker("foo", pytest.mark.foo(1))`, and returns the wrapped `~pytest.Mark`. Previously the only way to build a `default` was to instantiate `~pytest.Mark` directly, which is private and warns. - [#​13369](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13369): Improved the error from `pytest.RunResult.assert_outcomes` when a plugin changes or removes pytest's standard terminal summary, and documented how to isolate output-changing plugins. - [#​13431](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13431): Exposed `pytest.ParameterSet` as the type of the return value of `pytest.param()`. This can be used in type annotations and `isinstance` checks. - [#​13564](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13564): Issue a warning when fixtures are wrapped with a decorator that prevents correct discovery, including `@classmethod` above `@pytest.fixture` and `@staticmethod` above `@pytest.fixture`. Put `@pytest.fixture` above those decorators on test classes. - [#​14164](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14164): Exposed `pytest.Approx` as the type of the return value of `pytest.approx()`. This can be used in type annotations and `isinstance` checks. - [#​14463](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14463): Assertion diffs for mappings now match up keys the way the compared mappings match them themselves. Key comparison goes through the mappings' key views instead of plain sets of their keys, so a mapping with its own notion of key equivalence, such as case-insensitive header mappings, no longer reports its common keys as missing on either side. - [#​14523](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14523): Large assertion comparison diffs are now built lazily and capped to the truncation budget, so a huge diff is no longer formatted in full just to be truncated. As a consequence, the truncation footer no longer reports the exact number of hidden lines. - [#​14687](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14687): The default fd-level output capturing (`--capture=fd`) now skips reading the capture buffer for tests which produce no output, reducing per-test overhead in large test suites. - [#​14724](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14724): `--no-summary` now only applies directly to pytest's own summary. The flag no longer skips the `pytest_terminal_summary` hook, so third-party plugins (for example coverage) can still write their terminal summaries. - [#​14751](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14751): `parser.addini ` now also accepts type expressions for its `type` argument, in addition to the existing string tags: the plain Python types `str`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, a `Literal` of strings, and unions of these (for example `int | str` or `int | Literal["auto"]`). - [#​14754](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14754): `pytest.approx()` now rejects infinite relative tolerances for `datetime.timedelta` values with a clear `ValueError` instead of raising `OverflowError`. - [#​14791](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14791): The `junit_family`, `junit_logging`, `junit_duration_report`, `console_output_style`, `empty_parameter_set_mark`, `assertion_text_diff_style` and `tmp_path_retention_policy` configuration options are now registered with the set of values they accept: an invalid value now fails with a clean usage error instead of being silently ignored or crashing later, and `pytest --help` lists the accepted values. `config.getini ` now raises `pytest.UsageError` instead of `TypeError` or `ValueError` when the value read from the configuration file does not match the registered type, so a bad value is always reported as a short usage error message instead of an internal error traceback. Asking for an option name that was never registered still raises `ValueError`. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): `pytest.approx` now emits `pytest.PytestApproxDecimalToleranceWarning` when a `rel` or `abs` tolerance is given as a `float` that cannot be represented exactly for a `~decimal.Decimal` comparison, since such a tolerance is widened to the float's exact binary value. - [#​14675](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14675), [#​14953](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14953), [#​15153](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15153), [#​15132](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15132): The `truncation_limit_lines`, `truncation_limit_chars`, `max_warnings`, `verbosity_assertions`, `verbosity_test_cases`, `verbosity_subtests`, `tmp_path_retention_count`, `log_level`, `log_cli_level`, `log_file_level`,`log_auto_indent` and `faulthandler_timeout` configuration options now accept native integer (and, for `log_auto_indent`, boolean) values in TOML configuration files, while still accepting strings for backward compatibility. `log_file_mode` now reports invalid values as a usage error. - [#​15254](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15254): `tmp_path` and `TempPathFactory.mktemp ` no longer list the whole base temporary directory on every call, which made sessions with many temporary directories quadratically slow. Numbers are now handed out from a per-prefix counter, skipping names that already exist. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `Node.add_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.add_marker>` now stores a `~pytest.Mark` in `node.keywords`, matching what marks applied during collection store. Previously it stored a `~pytest.MarkDecorator`. - [#​9436](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9436): Avoided formatting tracebacks for tests marked with `xfail(run=False)`. #### Bug fixes - [#​10128](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10128): Configured warning filters now apply to warnings emitted by `pytest_configure` hooks. - [#​10210](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10210): `pytest.approx` now raises a `TypeError` for any nested container, not only for one of the same type as its parent. Previously `approx([{"k": 1}])` and `approx({"k": [1]})` were accepted and then compared unequal to every value, silently ignoring the tolerance, while `approx([[1]])` correctly reported that nesting is unsupported. - [#​10644](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10644): `monkeypatch.setattr()` no longer leaves a new entry in the instance `__dict__` when it patches an attribute that the instance inherits from its class. Previously `undo()` assigned the inherited value onto the instance, which shadowed the class attribute -- permanently freezing the result for descriptors that resolve dynamically. - [#​1139](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1139): Fixed tracebacks showing `???` instead of source lines for code compiled with a filename relative to a directory other than the current working directory -- e.g. compiled Cython modules, when running pytest from a subdirectory of the project root. The source lookup now falls back to searching `sys.path` for such filenames, as the standard `traceback` module does. - [#​11502](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11502): The `rootdir` is no longer derived from a configuration file that is not a regular file, such as `--config-file=/dev/null`. - [#​11783](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11783): Plugins installed in editable mode (`660`) are marked for assertion rewriting again. Such installs do not record the package's Python files in the distribution metadata, so pytest found nothing to rewrite and assertions inside the plugin lost their introspection. The plugin's entry point is now used to locate the package in that case. - [#​11933](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11933): `pytest.warns` no longer re-emits unmatched warnings with `module="warnings"`, which caused `module`-based warning filters to be applied to the wrong warnings. Since `warnings.WarningMessage` does not record the module a warning was emitted with, re-emitted warnings now use the standard `warnings.warn_explicit` default of deriving the module from the warning's filename. - [#​12175](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12175): `ExceptionInfo.exconly(tryshort=True) ` now strips the `AssertionError:` prefix of failed `assert` statements for `~pytest.ExceptionInfo` objects created by `pytest.raises`, and failures inside `unittest.TestCase.subTest` report the same short crash line as regular tests. - [#​12223](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12223): The `message` attribute of `` and `` elements in `--junitxml` reports is now shortened to whole lines within 500 characters. When something is dropped, it ends with a note pointing to the element text, which still holds the full report. Previously, very verbose assertion output (e.g. with `-vv`) produced attributes tens of thousands of characters long, which some XML parsers fail on. - [#​12307](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12307): Fixed truncation of long collections (lists, dicts, sets, etc.) in the "message" part of failed assertions (as in `assert condition, msg`) when using `-vv`: the message now uses the same unlimited repr as the rest of the assertion output, instead of eliding collection elements with `...`. - [#​12824](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12824): Custom command-line options now fail with a clear error when their implicit destination conflicts with an existing option, avoiding silent overrides of built-in options such as `-k`. - [#​13292](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13292): Fixed a stale rewritten module being used when a test file is modified twice within the same second without changing its size -- the pyc header could only record whole-second timestamps. The cache is now keyed on a hash of the source. - [#​14036](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14036): `__tracebackhide__` is now respected in `ExceptionGroup` tracebacks, both for the group itself and for its sub-exceptions. - [#​14189](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14189): Nested usage of `caplog.filtering ` no longer removes filters early if they were already present. - [#​14412](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14412): Fixed incorrect timing information for subtests and parent tests when `console_output_style = "times"`. - [#​14445](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14445): Assertion rewriting no longer evaluates walrus operator (`:=`) expressions more than once, which reported results the test never computed when the expression had side effects. An operand evaluated before a later walrus is now reported with the value it actually saw, so `assert value != identity(value := value.lower())` keeps Python's left-to-right order. - [#​14552](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14552): Fixed stale `co_filename` values after a test module or directory is moved. Assertion-rewrite caches are reused when the source hash still matches, and in-memory code objects are pointed at the current path. - [#​14586](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14586): Negative values passed to `log_auto_indent` now correctly fall back to no indentation, matching the documented behavior. - [#​14619](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14619): Fixed a crash in `pytest.mark.parametrize` when a non-sequence value is passed for a parameter set. It now provides a clear error message during collection. - [#​14635](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14635): Fixed fixture resolution failures when specifying multiple test paths on the command line that share common parent directories. Parametrized fixtures defined in a `conftest.py` could be silently dropped depending on the order of the specified paths. - [#​14637](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14637): Pytest now correctly skips identical trailing characters in assertion text diffs even when the compared strings differ at the beginning. - [#​14638](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14638): Top-level options in `pytest.toml` and `.pytest.toml` files now raise an error instead of being silently ignored when no `[pytest]` table is present. - [#​14683](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14683): Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1 where a conftest.py located in the rootdir was no longer visible to tests and doctests collected from *outside* the rootdir (for example when passing a parent directory of the rootdir as a collection argument, or setting `--rootdir` to a subdirectory). As a result, fixtures defined in such a conftest -- including `doctest_namespace` injections -- were not available, causing errors such as `NameError` in doctests. - [#​14700](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14700): Fixed an internal error on Python 3.12 when a doctest on a fixture-decorated function was skipped. - [#​14705](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14705): TOML configuration files passed via `-c` now also read their configuration from the `[pytest]` table, the one pytest's own configuration files use. The `[tool.pytest]` and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` tables such files were previously restricted to keep working; using both styles in one file is an error. - [#​14828](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14828): Exception groups raised from another exception now print their cause chain only once in the traceback output. - [#​14864](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14864): Fixed collection on Windows collecting the whole suite instead of the given path, on file systems which do not support file IDs (`st_ino` is `0` for every file, as seen for example on `sshfs-win`/WinFsp mounts). - [#​14884](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14884): `Cache.get()`, `Cache.set()` and `Cache.mkdir()` now reject keys that resolve outside the cache directory, and `--cache-show` ignores glob matches outside it. - [#​14909](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14909): Fixed `MonkeyPatch.delattr `, `MonkeyPatch.setitem ` and `MonkeyPatch.delitem ` recording a stale undo entry when the underlying mutation failed, which could cause spurious errors during teardown. The undo entry is now recorded only after the mutation succeeds, matching the behavior of `MonkeyPatch.setattr `. - [#​14912](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14912): `~pytest.PytestWarning` instances defined in `_pytest.deprecated` are no longer reused across `warnings.warn` calls, so warnings raised as errors (e.g. with `-W error`) no longer accumulate stale traceback frames from previous raises. - [#​14942](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14942): Fixed a regression in 9.1.0 that made collection very slow (quadratic) when many fixtures are defined with the same name. This can happen particularly when many tests are defined in separate classes which inherit from a base class which defines fixtures (the fixtures are repeated per class). - [#​15005](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15005): `pytest.approx` no longer treats finite `~decimal.Decimal` values outside the `float` range (such as `Decimal("1e400")`) as infinite, which made in-tolerance comparisons fail. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): Restored the tolerance shown by `pytest.approx` for `~decimal.Decimal` values, which since 9.0 displayed `???` for the default tolerance and reported the raw `rel` ratio instead of the absolute tolerance actually compared against. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): The failure message for `pytest.approx` comparisons of `~decimal.Decimal` collections no longer reports `Max absolute difference: -inf`, or crashes for mappings, when the `decimal.FloatOperation` trap is set. - [#​15006](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006): `pytest.approx` no longer raises `AttributeError` when comparing `numpy.ndarray` instances with `object` dtype, such as arrays of `~decimal.Decimal`. - [#​15032](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15032): Help texts for command-line options and configuration options now keep their indentation and blank lines. Previously each line was stripped before wrapping, so a wrapped list item was indistinguishable from a new one and blank lines were dropped; configuration option help lost its line breaks entirely. - [#​15043](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15043): Cache writes now emit `pytest.PytestCacheWarning` when writing or closing the cache file fails, consistent with errors opening the file. - [#​15052](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15052): Fixed possible off-by-one line numbers in `--fixtures` and `--fixtures-per-test` output. - [#​15145](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15145): With `console_output_style` set to `times`, durations just below a unit boundary are now shown in the next unit (e.g. `1.000ms` instead of `1000.0us`). - [#​15172](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15172): Assertion diffs now pretty-print the built-in `frozendict` (Python 3.15+) across multiple lines, similarly to how `dict` is displayed. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `-k` no longer matches attributes that end up in a test function's `__dict__` without being meant as keywords, such as pytest's own `pytestmark` attribute and the bookkeeping left behind by `functools.wraps` and `functools.lru_cache`. - [#​6750](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6750): Fix fixture argument discovery for custom collectors that pass bound methods to `pytest.Function`. - [#​6997](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6997): XFAIL reports from teardown phases now include the phase in the short test summary. - [#​7940](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7940): Fixed cleanup of temporary directories failing when subdirectories have their execute permission removed. - [#​8321](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8321): Fixed exception chains being duplicated in the traceback output when an exception in the chain (`__cause__`/`__context__`) has no traceback of its own, and that exception is itself linked to further exceptions. - [#​8914](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8914): Tests parametrized with higher-than-function scope are now reordered by parameter *value* rather than by parameter *index*, so that items using equal parameter values are grouped together and share a single fixture setup, even when they are parametrized by separate `@pytest.mark.parametrize ` calls. Previously, an expensive higher-scoped fixture could be set up and torn down repeatedly for the same parameter value. Unhashable parameter values (e.g. dicts) keep the previous index-based grouping behavior. As a consequence, the order in which parametrized tests run may change (fixture setup/teardown counts can only decrease, not increase). - [#​9924](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9924): Fixed doctest option flags leaking between docstrings after a failure, skip, or expected failure. #### Improved documentation - [#​10721](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10721): Replaced `setup.py` usage with `pyproject.toml` in `writing-plugins`. - [#​12658](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12658): Moved the fixture setup and finalizer hooks to the test running hooks section in the reference documentation. - [#​12857](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12857): Documented how `--confcutdir` affects initial `conftest.py` discovery. - [#​14157](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14157): Added the `pytest-flakefighters` plugin to the list of flaky test plugins in `plugins.rst`. Added flaky test papers published on the [Test FLARE](https://test-flare.github.io/) project to the list of flaky papers in `plugins.rst`. - [#​15127](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15127): Added guidance on typing yield fixtures, including annotating fixture functions with their generator type and fixture consumers with the yielded value type. - [#​15242](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15242): The `installation instructions ` and `install-package-with-pip` now show how to install pytest into a virtual environment with venv and pip, uv or virtualenv, and explain the `externally-managed-environment` error. - [#​4569](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569): `pytest --help`, the `-k` reference entry and `select-tests` no longer describe `-k` as a Python expression matched against test names only; `keyword expressions` now shows marker names being matched as well. The examples that looked up a marker use `Node.get_closest_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.get_closest_marker>` rather than `item.keywords`. - [#​9614](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9614): Clarified that `session.items` and `session.testscollected` exclude deselected tests in the `pytest_collection` documentation. #### Packaging updates and notes for downstreams - [#​11680](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11680): Source archives of arbitrary commits -- the tarballs GitHub serves under `/archive/`, not just the ones for tags -- can now be built into an sdist or a wheel with a correct version. A `.git_archival.txt` file, expanded by `git archive` via `export-subst`, carries the describe output that `setuptools-scm` would otherwise have to ask `git` for. The archival file deliberately omits `ref-names`. Recording it would make the content of an archive -- and therefore its checksum -- change whenever a branch that points at the archived commit is moved afterwards, which is how the equivalent tarballs of tagged releases became unstable for other projects. Describe output alone depends only on the commit and on the tags reachable from it. The archival file is not shipped in the sdist -- an sdist carries its version in its metadata, and the template is only ever expanded by `git archive`. Building pytest from a git checkout now requires `setuptools-scm >= 10.1`. - [#​9236](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9236): `pluggy>=1.6` is now required. Older pluggy versions stopped running the remaining hook wrapper teardowns once an old-style `hookwrapper` raised in its own teardown. The logging plugin's wrapper was left suspended, and when it was finalised later it detached the handler that `caplog` of a subsequent test was recording through, so that test saw no records. #### Contributor-facing changes - [#​14813](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14813): Added a systematic coverage matrix for assertion rewriting. - [#​14921](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14921): Added scripts/diff-assert-rewrite.py, which diffs the assert-rewritten form of a snippet between the plain source, this checkout and released pytest versions. - [#​15190](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15190): Fixed the documentation build with Pluggy 1.7 by ignoring a reference to its undocumented `DistFacade` compatibility class. #### Miscellaneous internal changes - [#​13888](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13888): `FixtureRequest.node ` is now explicitly annotated as returning `Any`, so strict pyright no longer reports it as `Unknown`. The return type stays deliberately broad, see `13888`. - [#​14758](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14758): Internal node ids (the `::`-separated strings identifying collected items, e.g. `path/to/test_file.py::TestClass::test_method[param]`) are now represented internally by a single structured `~_pytest.nodeid.NodeId` dataclass instead of being repeatedly re-parsed as plain strings. The public `nodeid: str` attribute on nodes and reports is unchanged and remains fully backward compatible for plugins.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/ruff (ruff)</summary>

### [`v0.17.4`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0174)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/compare/0.17.3...0.17.4)

Released on 2026-11-05.

##### Preview features

- \[`flake8-logging-format`] Avoid behavior changes and syntax errors in fixes (`G004`) ([#​27419](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27419))
- \[`security`] Implement `tarfile-ignore-zeros-true` ([#​28680](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28680))

##### Bug fixes

- Accept a bare raise before a semicolon ([#​29761](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29761))
- Allow match identifiers after a semicolon ([#​29760](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29760))
- Fix panic on BOM-prefixed files in diagnostic renderer ([#​30017](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30017))
- \[`flake8-simplify`] Report collapsible `elif` clauses after a multi-statement `if` branch (`SIM102`) ([#​29814](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29814))

##### Rule changes

- Show more nonprinting characters in diagnostic fix diffs ([#​30062](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30062))

##### Performance

- Coalesce source slices when formatting attributes ([#​29841](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29841))
- Collect return statements with a statement-only visitor ([#​29911](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29911))
- \[`pyflakes`] Defer value comparisons for repeated dictionary keys (`F601`, `F602`) ([#​29739](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29739))
- Format node fields directly when comment handling is unnecessary ([#​29853](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29853))
- Reduce formatter source-slice overhead ([#​29855](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29855))
- Reuse a callee's qualified name across lint rules ([#​29916](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29916))
- Skip invalid string character checks when the source contains none ([#​29883](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29883))
- Use a Bloom filter for formatter comment lookups ([#​29852](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29852))
- Use a concrete buffer for ordinary writes ([#​29819](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29819))

##### CLI

- Give `NO_COLOR` precedence in Ruff and ty diagnostics ([#​29898](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29898))
- Honor `CLICOLOR=0` in Ruff and ty diagnostics ([#​29910](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29910))

##### Documentation

- Correct the documented `version` and `src` defaults for `ruff-action` ([#​29880](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29880))
- \[`flake8-bugbear`] Make `B014` example error out-of-the-box ([#​29941](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29941))
- \[`flake8-no-pep420`] Document preview behavior (`INP001`) ([#​29764](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29764))
- \[`isort`] Expand `I001` documentation ([#​29843](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29843))

##### Other changes

- \[syntax-errors] Extend `__debug__` write check to attribute targets ([#​27908](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27908))

body:
Step 3 of the GitHub runner exit, part 1 of 2. Adds `hassfest` and `hacs` jobs to Forgejo ci.yml, beside GitHub's hassfest.yml.

- hassfest: Home Assistant's own image, pinned by digest through the image mirror, copied in with docker create + cp (a bind mount from the job container mounts nothing).
- hacs: the HACS action image, pinned by digest, run against the GitHub mirror at this exact commit after waiting for the push mirror to carry it. INPUT_REPOSITORY is set so the full 10-check set runs (without it HACS treats the run as a fork PR and runs 5); the job fails if fewer than 10 ran.
- Proven locally: hassfest valid on main and fails on a broken manifest; HACS 10/10 at edcef22 (same 10 checks as GitHub run 43802314100).

Not required checks and not in the `macos` job's needs. Part 2 deletes hassfest.yml (plus its GITHUB_ONLY entry, retry watch-list entry, macos-scope regex + test, ci-split.md bullet) after 5 main pushes green on both.

dreame-valetudo has no Home Assistant surface, so this step has no sibling change (VARIANCE.md HACS row).

body:
Shadow of the two GitHub arm64 legs on our own native arm64 runner. Nothing GitHub does changes, and nothing here can fail a release or the stable gate.

- `release-arm64.yml` (tag push): builds the arm64 assets the way `release-linux-arm64.yml` does, publishes nothing, and compares them with the copies GitHub appends (`packaging/compare-arch-build.sh`: package metadata, file lists with modes and link targets, signatures, archive contents).
- `install-matrix-arm64.yml` (dispatched by `publish.yml` beside the other two matrices): the same four arm64 install shards.
- Both are their own workflows so a queued or slow arm64 job can never hold the publish run or the install-matrix run the stable gate reads. Every step that can fail is continue-on-error; the verdict is the `SHADOW-VERDICT` line.

Proved on a throwaway repo against the current candidates (dreame-valetudo v0.3.0-rc.49, whiskerless v0.2.0-rc.76): both builds `VERDICT agree` with GitHub's assets; install shards all pass except dreame-valetudo's bottle-pour, because the tap carries no bottle for rc.49 (GitHub's own rc.49 matrix never reached its shards: its wait found the macOS .pkg missing).

The flip (the upload replaces the compare, GitHub's copies go) is a later PR once a real release candidate shows both agree.

body:
Shadow of GitHub's `ci-macos.yml` and `formula-macos.yml` on our own Mac: macOS 15 (the floor) and the newest macOS, each in its own VM. Nothing GitHub does changes.

- `macos.yml` runs on every push to every branch, keyed per commit like GitHub's (cancelled only on Renovate branches), with the same `macos-scope.sh` skip for Linux-only Renovate branches. No pull_request trigger, so a fork's code never runs on these machines.
- The Homebrew formula smoke runs first, while the VM is as clean as a user's Mac, then the native tests, shellcheck and the release-script tests.
- Every check is continue-on-error; the verdict is the `SHADOW-VERDICT tier=... ci=... formula=...` line. The one step allowed to fail the job is the Python setup, so nothing pip-installs into the image's own interpreter.
- setup-python's macOS build expects GitHub's tool cache path and an admin runner user; the job provides the path and hands the framework it installs to the job user between the two attempts.

On this branch both VMs ran green: SHADOW-VERDICT ci=success formula=success on floor and current.

The switch (GitHub's copies go, the gates read this) is a later PR after about a week of agreement.

body:
Closes #178

Large diff: mostly deletions. The GitHub CI workflows go, the vendored helpers that bridged to them are replaced by the project-rules v0.3.0 re-vendor, and their invariant tests go with them.

**Contributing.** Issues and pull requests go to Forgejo, where anyone can sign in with a GitHub account; the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror. CONTRIBUTING describes the AGit flow (`git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main -o topic=…`). CI does not run on a pull request sent that way: the runners are trusted with release credentials. A maintainer reads the change and opens it again from a branch here, which runs the whole suite.

**CI on our own runners only.**
- `macos.yml` is the macOS gate, on macOS 15 and the newest macOS. It runs on push to every branch, never on pull_request, and swallows no failures (only the setup-python fallback stays tolerated).
- Its two jobs replace `CI / macos (pull_request)` as required checks on `main`: `macOS / macOS floor (macos-15-vm) (push)` and `macOS / macOS current (macos-27-vm) (push)`. Branch protection is updated when this merges.
- `ci.yml` loses the `macos` job that waited on GitHub's run.
- The release and prerelease `mirror-gate` becomes `macos-gate`. It runs `check-forgejo-ci.sh <sha> macos.yml` with no credential, and passes only a run whose every job succeeded, so a scoped-out Renovate run cannot qualify a cut.
- The candidate gate asks Forgejo only. It reads `install-matrix.yml` (amd64) and refuses to trust a shadow matrix: `install-matrix-arm64.yml` swallows its own failures, so a test now fails if it is ever listed in `INSTALL_MATRIX_WORKFLOWS`.
- Deleted: `.github/workflows/ci-pr.yml`, `ci-macos.yml`, `formula-macos.yml` and `retry-infra-failures.yml` and `hassfest.yml` (`ci.yml` already runs hassfest and HACS from their images). With them go the vendored `check-mirror-ci.sh`, `triage-infra-failure.py`, `forgejo-preflight.sh` and their tests.
- Docs (`docs/design/ci-split.md`, `packaging/README.md`) and invariant tests are rewritten to match. The new tests check that `macos.yml` never runs on pull_request, swallows nothing and covers both macOS legs. They also check that the release gate requires a fully green run on the exact commit, and that the candidate gate lists every install-matrix workflow.

**Release side, until the release-in-house PR lands.**
- The re-vendor removes `forgejo-preflight.sh`, so this PR deletes its step from the GitHub release workflows that remain. Its only reader was the infra-retry workflow, which goes too.
- The candidate gate now reads Forgejo only and cannot see GitHub's macOS and arm64 install legs. So `release.yml` refuses a stable cut while `.github/workflows/install-matrix.yml` exists; a test pins that refusal. Prereleases are unaffected.
- The release-in-house PR moves those legs here and removes both the file and the refusal.

**Also tightened.**
- The AGit trust-gate test covers every job of a pull-request workflow, with recorded exceptions, not only the jobs that already had a head-repository check.
- The ref check on the gated macOS workflow is case-insensitive, so a script reading `$GITHUB_REF` is caught too.

Checks run here: ruff, mypy, the full pytest suite, `tests/release/*.sh`, `shellcheck-all.sh`. cx review raised the release-side gaps above (fixed by the preflight removal and the refusal); qx reviewed the follow-ups.

title: ci: run CI on our own runners only, and send contributions to Forgejo

body:
Forgejo treats an AGit pull request (pushed to `refs/for/main`, no fork needed) as untrusted and holds its runs for approval, but its payload reports this repository as the head (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), so the existing fork gate let it through. When a maintainer acts on an outsider's PR (reopen), Forgejo 17 runs this branch's workflows, with secrets, against the PR's commit (services/actions/trust.go). Outside contributors are about to be able to sign in with GitHub and open AGit PRs, so the gate now also requires `github.event.pull_request.flow == 0`.

Proof (throwaway SisyphusMD/agit-guard-proof-20261116): an AGit PR's payload has `flow=1` and head repo = base repo, and the gated job was skipped (run 37485); a branch PR has `flow=0` and the gated job ran (run 37486).

Outside PRs get CI when a maintainer, after reading the diff, pushes the head to a branch here.

New test `test_trust_gates_also_exclude_agit_pull_requests` fails on the old ci.yml (all ten gated jobs) and passes now.
