title: Setup fails on HA 2026.11: RestoreStateData has no attribute last_states

body:
_Recreated from GitHub pull request [#17](https://github.com/SisyphusMD/whiskerless/pull/17), opened by @CryingPecan on 2026-11-06, when the GitHub copy became read-only._

_This is a record of the pull request, not the pull request itself: its commits are kept in the maintainer's archive and were not pushed here._

---

## The bug

On Home Assistant **2026.11.0** every config entry fails in `async_setup_entry` and all entities go unavailable:

```
File "custom_components/whiskerless/__init__.py", line 560, in async_setup_entry
    _recheck_sightings(hass, entry)
File "custom_components/whiskerless/__init__.py", line 241, in _recheck_sightings
    last_states = restore_state.async_get(hass).last_states
AttributeError: 'RestoreStateData' object has no attribute 'last_states'
```

2026.11 replaced `RestoreStateData.last_states` (one dict keyed by entity id) with `last_states_by_entity_id` and `last_states_by_entity_registry_id`, read through a new `async_get_stored_state(entity_id)`. The integration reaches into the old dict in four places:

| Where | What it reads the cache for |
|---|---|
| `__init__.py` hopper seed | the restored fill gauge |
| `__init__.py` `_recheck_sightings` / `_reproved` | past reports that still prove a capability |
| `__init__.py` entity rename | moving the cache entry to the new entity id |
| `coordinator.py` latching-sensor seed | the restored `on`/`off` |

The first one that runs raises before the coordinator exists, so nothing after it happens. `main` and `v0.2.0-rc.74` both have these lines.

## Seen live

Two robots on rc.74. Home Assistant updated to 2026.11.0 on 2026-11-05 and both entries went to `setup_error` at the first start. The robots stayed connected to the broker and kept cycling; Home Assistant just could not see them. With this change applied to the installed copy and a core restart, both entries load on 2026.11.0 and every sensor is back. The entries pass through `setup_retry` for about a minute while each robot answers, same as before.

One side effect worth knowing: no live alert fired during the outage. Entities that *start* unavailable never make the transition an "offline" trigger waits for.

## The fix

`coordinator.stored_state(hass, entity_id)` does the lookup: through `async_get_stored_state` where core has it, through the dict where it does not. The hopper seed, the sighting re-check and the latching-sensor seed all go through it.

The rename is the one place that *wrote* to the dict. 2026.11 keys the cache by registry id, so a renamed entity keeps its stored state there without help. The hand move now only happens on a core that still has the dict.

No behavior change on older cores.

## Tests

`pytest-homeassistant-custom-component` still pins `homeassistant==2026.10.4`, so the suite cannot run on a real 2026.11 yet. The new tests in `tests/integration/test_restore_cache_layouts.py` present the 2026.11 layout to the integration by swapping the `restore_state` reference its two modules hold. Core keeps its own reference, so Home Assistant's own restore path is untouched. On a test core that already has the new layout the fixture passes the real object through.

- the lookup uses the accessor when core has one, and the dict when it does not
- a restored fill gauge still proves a hopper under the 2026.11 layout (the two reads that took setup down)
- a latched sensor still restores under it
- a rename does not reach for the old dict under it

Reverting any one call site makes the matching test fail with the same `AttributeError`.

Run locally on Python 3.13 / Home Assistant 2026.2.3:

```
ruff check        All checks passed
mypy              no issues in 29 source files
pytest tests/integration --cov --cov-fail-under=99
                  213 passed, coverage 99.80%
```

_@CryingPecan on GitHub, 2026-11-14:_

Closing as superseded: fc6898b on main fixes the same `last_states` removal, and it shipped in v0.2.0-rc.75. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

The LR4 classifier currently treats unrecognized command types as no-ops, which lets them through by default. Require `allow_dangerous` for unknown types and add regression tests showing that known no-ops still pass and never-send commands remain blocked. comments.body: Claude (session f565c0c9) has this, on branch fix/218-unknown-command-opt-in.

Technical call: Every type byte other than 01 (read) and 02 (write) is unknown and needs allow_dangerous; the whole byte is read, so 0x12A00000 is no longer taken for a type-2 write. An unknown type aimed at a never-send opcode, register or panel value is NEVER, so the opt-in cannot unlock a reset. "Known no-ops" are the writes already proven to be discarded (0x1A-0x1C) and stay SAFE. Hazard.NOOP is removed and CommandType.NOOP becomes UNKNOWN. Why: Only types 1 and 2 were ever tested; "anything else = no-op" came from the initial commit with no trial behind it, and the safety module already refuses untested commands on cost, not proof. #188 asks for this rule from day one.

Decided by: Claude, 2026-11-19.

Audit the LR4 settings that whiskerless allows at any value. Keep unconditional writes for settings whose full range is verified. For the rest, allow verified values by default and require `allow_dangerous` for unverified values. Add regression tests at the boundaries and confirm that never-send commands remain blocked.

comments.body: Claude (session 97baacb9) has this, on branch fix/219-verified-value-ranges.

Technical call: A settings write is SAFE only inside its verified range, checked on the full 16-bit value; anything outside it is DANGEROUS and needs allow_dangerous. "Verified" means the value lies in the setting's defined domain (an enum, a percentage, minutes since midnight, a seven-day mask, or the range the app offers) and live writes inside that domain were read back. The ranges:

| Reg | Setting | SAFE values | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x05` | isDebugModeActive | none | no write recorded (#91) |
| `0x0E` | panel brightness | each byte 0–100 | written at 5 and stock 40/50; HA ships 0–100 (see the question below) |
| `0x16` | clean-cycle wait | 3–30 | written at 3, 7 and 20; the app's span |
| `0x17` | keypad lockout | 0–1 | both written |
| `0x18` | night-light mode | 0–2 | enum, all three written |
| `0x19` | night-light brightness | 0–100 | percentage, `0x63`/`0x64` written |
| `0x1A` | panel sleep mode (discarded) | 0–1 | discarded writes at 0/1 |
| `0x1B`/`0x1C` | panel sleep/wake (discarded) | 0–1439 | discarded writes inside the day |
| `0x1D` | weekday sleep mask | 0–`0x7F` | seven-day mask; `0x00`, `0x01` and `0x7F` written |
| `0x1E`–`0x2B` | weekday sleep/wake | 0–1439 | distinct per-day writes read back |

The never-send checks still run first, so no value or opt-in unlocks them. The builders keep their clamps, so `whiskerless set` refuses an out-of-range value up front and says so, instead of quietly sending a different value. Why: These registers took any 16-bit value, including `0x05`, which has never been written. Anything past the tested range is a write nobody has seen land, and #188 needs the same rule per model.

Decided by: Claude, 2026-11-19.

Decision: Panel brightness stays sendable at 0-100 per level without allow_dangerous. Why: It is what the Home Assistant sliders already offer, and brightness is reversible; only 5, 40 and 50 have been written.

Decided by: Cody, 2026-11-20.

Done in #240, merged as 4df4531. Every LR4 settings register now has a verified range. A value outside it needs allow_dangerous, debug mode (0x05) has no safe value, panel brightness is checked per level (0-100, per the decision above), and never-send targets stay refused at any value. `whiskerless set` refuses an out-of-range value before it connects. The current guide asks the person setting up the broker to translate a generic Mosquitto example into Home Assistant settings. body:
Closes #218

The safety guard read only the second digit of a command's two-digit type byte. A type byte ending in 1 (`0x11`, `0x21`, …) was classified as a read and sent with no opt-in, so `0x11A30000`, a reset-class opcode, went out as `safe`. One ending in 2 inherited full write rules. Every other type was taken for a firmware no-op and also sent without opt-in, although only types `01` and `02` have ever been tried on a robot. The one unknown field that has been tried, the panel press type, was performed rather than ignored.

Now the whole type byte is parsed. Any type other than `01` or `02` is `dangerous` and needs `allow_dangerous`. A never-send opcode, register or panel value is refused at any type, so the opt-in cannot unlock a reset. Writes already proven to be discarded (`0x1A`–`0x1C`) stay `safe`. A raw panel-register write with an unknown type is still sent at most once.

`Hazard.NOOP` is removed and `CommandType.NOOP` is renamed `CommandType.UNKNOWN`. Nothing in the library or integration used them; the CHANGELOG lists the change under breaking changes. The protocol, codec, safety and contributor docs now describe the type as two digits and name the new refusal.

The new tests reject `0x11A30000` and `0x11AC0000` even with `allow_dangerous`, reject `0x03180001` without it, classify `0x12A00000` as `dangerous` rather than a safe report macro, and require at-most-once delivery for `0x12010201`. Each failed against `main`. The design is recorded on #218 (comment 39162).

- a panel brightness level over 100 in either byte
- `set` connecting for a write the guard refuses

A test that pins the range table whole fails if a register is added at any value or dropped. Never-send targets are checked at several values with `allow_dangerous`. Every Home Assistant entity range and the integration test values are inside the new ranges.
